newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares recoup losses, AEX back above 800.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares recoup losses, AEX back above 800.

text.p: Dutch shares regained most of their early losses on Thursday, closing marginally weaker after the key AEX index sank to test support at 800 points.
The blue-chip index closed just 0.33 points lower at 804.62 after dipping briefly below 800 to 798.74 points.

The market made a slow start, with most traders awaiting results from financial services giant ING Group, which were released towards midday. The group made a first quarter net profit of 891 million guilders, up 21 percent on last year.
Analysts said figures looked good but profit-taking took its toll on the shares and they ended 1.30 guilders easier at 86.90.
"These figures are very nice. Earnings per share were exactly as we had expected, and the quality of the results is very good," said Bart van Feen of IRIS Research.
The share weakness spread to sector rival ABN AMRO which topped the volume list, losing 20 cents at 36.00 guilders.

Dutch-Belgian financial group Fortis Amev, which announced a 30 percent jump in first quarter profits on Wednesday also fell back, ending 1.80 down at 80.50 guilders. The company also had an upbeat forecast for the year ahead.
Dealers explained the falls by saying financials had had a good run and a bout of profit-taking was to be expected.
But dealers drew some comfort from the index holding above chart support at 800 points, although there were few signs of it moving substantially higher in the short term.
"The price is pausing within the uptrend," ING Barings Research said in a market comentary, adding that horizontal support could be expected at around the 800 level.
